scope: 2016 base/core multiplayer; no Automa, expansions, promos, or optional variants

key_findings.finding: Independently checked every expected answer against the complete extracted rulebook, including the specific source passages cited in the key. No material factual correction to any of the 45 expected answers is required. The key correctly handles attack-versus-defense popularity loss, worker-only displacement versus combat, lake cargo, encounter/Factory timing, fixed Factory card selection, objective timing, sixth-star interruption, scoring tiers, and the six structure tiles.

key_findings.source: Rulebook PDF p. 24: ENCOUNTERS instructions and concluding DESIGNER'S NOTE
key_findings.finding: The bank does not elicit the explicit public presentation procedure for an encounter. The player must show the artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud; the page also explicitly states that encounter cards are shown to all players when drawn. Q15 asks timing, location, costs and bonuses, while Q37 limits its information question to coins, combat cards and objectives. Their current keys permit an answer that never mentions the encounter's visibility. This is a distinct mandatory information procedure, not a cosmetic wording change or another scenario combining covered rules.

key_findings.source: Rulebook PDF pp. 19 and 29; source-only page renders visually inspected
key_findings.finding: All six structure tile diagrams support Q40/Q41, including the different maximum payout of the on-tunnels tile and combined farm/tundra counting. The p. 29 popularity diagram confirms the 13-18 upper scoring tier, resolving p. 28's textual reference to 13-17. Q20/Q39 correctly score 18 popularity in the top tier.

Did not propose extra questions for the combat deck's printed value distribution (component composition), encounter reference numbers (external-reference metadata), character biographies, achievement-sheet signatures (commemoration), strategy tips, or the excluded Delay of Game variant. Initial shuffling/placement of the three ordinary decks is a literal unelicited setup detail, but a separate question whose sole novelty is to shuffle and place those decks would be low-value setup padding. The public encounter procedure has a meaningful privacy outcome and warrants a distinct question.

Did not propose additional questions for optional bottom-action coins, Mill production without actual workers, worker/mech transport order, same-action enlist bonuses, Factory ability interactions, or interrupted movement after the final combat star. Existing Q03/Q05/Q10-Q12/Q16/Q19/Q23 already elicit their governing rules; merely selecting a fresh numerical example or combining them would not establish novelty. The source does not separately spell out a newly enlisted Enlist recruit's same-action case, so no new source-defined branch was invented for it.

proposed_additions.question: When you draw an encounter card, may you keep it private? What must you show or read aloud to the other players?
proposed_additions.key: The encounter card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud, then read through its costs and benefits and choose an option. The rules do not require reading every option aloud.
source: Rulebook PDF p. 24, ENCOUNTERS: Show the art to the other players and read the thematic text (the text in all caps) out loud.
Rulebook PDF p. 24, concluding DESIGNER'S NOTE: encounter cards are shown to all players when drawn.
proposed_additions.novelty: Distinct mandatory public-information procedure. Q15 does not ask encounter visibility or presentation, Q37 asks only coins/combat cards/objectives, and no expected answer in Q01-Q45 states this procedure. The tested outcome is whether a player may hide a drawn encounter from the table, not a changed quantity, cosmetic rewording, or mechanical combination.

limitations: Read only the complete extracted rulebook, source PDF/source-only page renders, and expanded-v3 questions.json and answer-key.json. Did not read summaries, reader answers or grades, coverage-ledger stopping conclusions, or other reviewer reports.
This review is independent of prior zero-addition passes. One qualifying uncovered procedure remains, so it does not certify saturation of the 45-question bank.
